newsitem.title: SPAIN: Strike called off at Spain's Inespal plants.
newsitem.headline: Strike called off at Spain's Inespal plants.

text.p: Strikes scheduled for Thursday at Spain's state-owned aluminum producer Inespal have been cancelled, a spokeswoman for Inespal said.
"There haven't been any strikes. They were cancelled," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
General workers union UGT said the union had maintained the strike at a national level but had been left for individual plants to decide whether to adhere to it.
A government pledge to discuss with workers plans to sell the group to Aluminum Co of America (Alcoa) was behind the plants' decision cancel the strike, a union official told Reuters.

Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales (SEPI), which controls Inespal, said talks with Alcoa were ongoing. Last February, Alcoa and SEPI signed a preliminary agreement for Alcoa to buy Inespal's main businesses by the end of 1997.
The deal would not include the sale of Inespal Conversion in Linares nor the factory at Ferroperfil. These were the last two plants to cancel strikes.
